title: Hope, not fear
hookLine: Christian hope is trust that God finishes what he begins (Philippians 1:6)

lines: A SENTENCE WITH NO DOUBT IN IT.
cards: The letter was written in chains. Paul tells the church at Philippi that his "bonds in Christ are manifest in all the palace."
He writes as a man who might live or die; a few lines later he weighs both, and says he's torn. You'd expect a letter like that to open with worry, or a request for help.
Instead, almost the first thing he writes is a sentence with no doubt in it at all, about somebody else's unfinished life. Today's word is what some Christians say all of Revelation is meant to give.

teach.h: HE WHICH HATH BEGUN WILL PERFORM IT.
teach.b: First, the sentence: "Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ." Perform, in the old English, means carry it through to the end.
The confidence isn't in the Philippians, still a work in progress, or in Paul, in prison. It rests on the one who began. Second, hope isn't the same as optimism.

Paul in bonds isn't forecasting good news; he says plainly, "to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain." Hebrews puts it this way: "Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen."

teach.h: HOPE THAT IS SEEN IS NOT HOPE.
teach.b: And Paul tells the Romans, "hope that is seen is not hope." Hope looks past what can be seen yet, to who holds the ending. Third, hope and fear.
Revelation can be read as a book of threats, and some people have met it that way. But this block kept arriving at the same places: all things new, open gates, healing leaves, come, Lord Jesus.
The first letter of John says, "There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear." Fear asks what will go wrong. Hope asks who is finishing the story.
Fourth, unfinished people. Paul isn't embarrassed that the Philippians are half-built. He expects it.
Some Christians bring this verse to people in the middle of things: a recovery, a grief, a slow change that hasn't arrived. The work isn't done. On Paul's account, it will be.

how: Christians name hope among faith, hope and love (1 Corinthians 13:13), and some memorize Philippians 1:6 or pray it for people going through a long, unfinished season.

o: trust that the one who began a good work will finish it
a cheerful guess that things will turn out fine
a wish for something you know won't really happen

games.q: hope, not fear — tap the pairs.
p: carry it through to the end

s: Paul wrote "he which hath begun a good work" while free and comfortable
his "bonds in Christ are manifest in all the palace."
in Philippians 1:6, the confidence rests on the one who began the work
"he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it."
hope, in these letters, means expecting things to go well
"hope that is seen is not hope": it looks past what can be seen yet.

games.q: you're Paul, in bonds, not sure whether you'll live or die. you're writing to a young church you love. how do you open?
o: with a warning that everything is falling apart.
with confidence that the one who began a good work in them will finish it.
with a request that they get you out.
games.why: "being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it." no doubt, from chains.

practice: Let one worry about something unfinished come up, your health, a child, your work, yourself, without rehearsing it.
Then look in that same place for something already begun, a first step, a small mercy, someone who showed up, and hold it beside the fear without needing the fear to disappear.
If you pray, rest on Paul's words, he which hath begun a good work; if not, keep both in view and breathe.

wordCard.voice: Hope. Not a guess that things will turn out fine, but trust, written from chains, that the one who began a good work will carry it through.

orig.note: Greek: hope, expectation. the word Paul uses for hope, as in "hope that is seen is not hope", Romans 8:24.

carryVoice: Your line: he will finish it. Hope rests on the one who began. See you tomorrow.
